sampleData.title: The Quiet Rebuild: How Coastal Towns Are Rewriting Their Own Flood Plans
sampleData.deck: A season of record rainfall pushed a dozen small towns to stop waiting on state guidance and start drafting their own resilience rules — with mixed, instructive results.
sampleData.author: Mara Ilves

sections.heading: A season that changed the calculus
paragraphs: By the time the third storm system stalled over the delta in July, the town council in Harlow Point had already exhausted its emergency repair budget for the fiscal year.
What followed was not a request for more state aid, but a decision to write the town's own building setback rules — a full year ahead of the state's own revision cycle.

figure.caption: Harlow Point's harbor road, closed for the second time this year after the June storm surge.

sections.heading: Borrowing from the neighbors, cautiously
paragraphs: Town planners across the region have started comparing notes informally, trading draft ordinances the way they once traded snowplow routes.
The approach is not without friction: a setback rule that makes sense on a barrier island reads very differently to a town built along a tidal river.
Even so, three of the five towns interviewed for this piece adopted language lifted nearly verbatim from a neighboring jurisdiction's 2025 ordinance.

figure.caption: Modelled surge depth for the Lower Delta district under the town's own revised 100-year assumption.

sections.heading: What the insurers are watching
paragraphs: Regional insurers say they are tracking these local rewrites closely, since a stricter local setback can move a parcel out of the highest-risk pricing tier well before any federal map update catches up.
That incentive is quietly doing more to drive adoption than any state grant program has managed in a decade.

figure.caption: The consortium's draft template, marked up by three towns before its first reading.

pullQuotes.quote: We stopped waiting for the map to catch up with the water.
pullQuotes.attribution: Dana Whitfield, Harlow Point town council

pullQuotes.quote: The neighboring towns' ordinances were the fastest first draft we ever had.
